actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -347,2 +347,36 @@
-    digest = sha256(sha256(v).digest()).digest()
-    return b58encode(v + digest[:4], alphabet)
+    digest = sha256(sha256(v).digest()).digest()
+    v = v + digest[:4]
+
+    # Same as b58encode, inlined to save a call per encode
+    origlen = len(v)
+    v = v.lstrip(b'\0')
+    newlen = len(v)
+
+    i = int.from_bytes(v, 'big')
+
+    tables = _encode_tables.get(alphabet)
+    if tables is None:
+        if len(_encode_tables) >= 128:
+            _encode_tables.clear()
+        tables = _encode_tables[alphabet] = _get_base58_encode_tables(alphabet)
+    pairs, sq, big, big3, zero = tables
+    parts = []
+    while i >= big3:
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq])
+    if i >= big:
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        rem3, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq])
+    elif i:
+        parts += pairs[i % sq], pairs[i // sq]
+    parts.reverse()
+    return zero * (origlen - newlen) + b''.join(parts).lstrip(zero)

--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -391,2 +391,40 @@
-    result = b58decode(v, alphabet, autofix=autofix)
-    payload = result[:-4]
+    # Same as b58decode, inlined to save a call per decode
+    v = v.rstrip()
+    if isinstance(v, str):
+        v = v.encode('ascii')
+
+    plans = _decode_plans_autofix if autofix else _decode_plans
+    plan = plans.get(alphabet)
+    if plan is None:
+        if len(plans) >= 128:
+            plans.clear()
+        plan = plans[alphabet] = _get_base58_decode_plan(alphabet, autofix)
+    zero, table, merges = plan
+
+    origlen = len(v)
+    v = v.lstrip(zero)
+    newlen = len(v)
+    if table is None:
+        acc = b58decode_int(v, alphabet=alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+    else:
+        digits = v.translate(table)
+        if 255 in digits:
+            bad = v[digits.index(255)]
+            raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(bad)))
+        acc = int.from_bytes(digits, 'big')
+        bits = (len(digits) - 1).bit_length()
+        if bits < 12:
+            merge = merges[bits]
+            if merge is None:
+                merge = merges[bits] = _get_base58_decode_merge(
+                    len(alphabet), bits)
+        else:
+            merge = _get_base58_decode_merge(len(alphabet), bits)
+        steps, last_shift, last_factor = merge
+        for shift, mask, factor in steps:
+            acc -= (acc >> shift & mask) * factor
+        acc -= (acc >> last_shift) * last_factor
+
+    result = acc.to_bytes(origlen - newlen + (acc.bit_length() + 7) // 8,
+                          'big')
+    payload = result[:-4]

actions.reason: I tried inlining the b58encode and b58decode bodies into b58encode_check and b58decode_check to save two Python calls per check round trip. Outputs were identical, but every metric got worse: check_ir ratio 1.0138, encode_ir 1.0171, decode_ir 1.0145. Encode and decode never run the new code, yet they rose by about the same amount, so the extra cost is in loading the larger module, not in the calls themselves. The source appears to be compiled on each benchmark run, which makes every added line of code cost instructions. What inlining saves per call is smaller than that load cost. Earlier attempts to trim the check wrapper on this tip also stayed under the 1% bar. I don't see an honest change to this path that clears 1%, so I'm stopping without a candidate.

journal.text:
Test agent here. Same bytes out was the bar. I inlined the b58encode and b58decode bodies into b58encode_check and b58decode_check. The idea was to save two Python calls per check round trip. Two edits in base58/__init__.py, 76 lines in all.

Outputs were identical. The numbers went the wrong way. check_ir went from 179950960 to 182435325, ratio 1.0138. The bar was 0.9900. encode_ir rose to ratio 1.0171 and decode_ir to ratio 1.0145. The sandbox rejected it with no improvement. I did not submit a candidate.

Encode and decode never touch the new code, yet they rose by about the same amount. So I think the extra cost comes from loading a larger module, not from the calls. That is a belief, not measured yet. The two saved calls are a small tide under a bigger swell.

Next I will read lineage_bench.py again to see how much import and setup it counts. Then I will look for a smaller change inside the per-character divmod loop.
